data.aboutMe:
I’d be happy to offer some advice to help you experience a different and perhaps more authentic side of Japan.

However, I should mention that I’m probably not the best person to ask about Tokyo, Osaka, or Kyoto. I’m often asked about these cities, but honestly, I don’t have much more information than what you can easily find online. They are also not my favorite places in Japan.

Japan has so much more to offer beyond these famous destinations.

If Shibuya Crossing and other well-known tourist attractions are what you’re looking for, you’ll probably find much better and more up-to-date information online. Shibuya, in particular, is actually one of the places I personally try to avoid!

What I’m much more interested in is helping travelers who want to discover Japan beyond the usual tourist route — smaller cities, countryside, regional towns, hot springs, local food, beautiful scenery, and places where you can experience a different side of Japanese life.

I would probably leave Sapporo off that list as well. It’s a nice city, of course, but if your goal is to experience regional Japan, I personally feel that it has more in common with large cities like Tokyo and Osaka.

But if you’re thinking about traveling somewhere outside the usual Tokyo–Kyoto–Osaka route, please feel free to ask me.

I may know something useful, and if I do, I’ll be happy to share it with you.

I'm actually so cool that I can afford to be weird and still be pretty cool.

A web programmer. Very easygoing person, little bit lazy. Love nature, animals, kids, peace, liberty, music, art, heritage architecture and photograph. 
I like various thinking and cultures.

I'm a friendly and open-minded person.

I lived in Nara until 18, then in Kyoto for 7 years,  in Yamaguchi 10 months, Saitama 2 months, Kanagawa 4 years,  and now live Meguro, Tokyo.  My area is quiet. It's two stops from Shibuya Station.  There are supermarkets and a lot of restaurants nearby.
I work in Kanda,  next to Tokyo Central Station. 

I like to travel, and as I have visited all prefectures in Japan, I'd like to visit more foreign countries. 
In fact, I was very shy in the past, I couldn't talk to others from me. In 2012, I travelled alone in Spain. It was my first time to travel alone abroad, and my first time to visit Europe. I was afraid before the trip, but after all, I really enjoyed the time talking with locals, seeing what I had never seen, driving in a different country, and so on. After that I like to travel more. 

I like to eat and drink. I usually go to eat and drink in Ginza, Shinjuku, and Ebisu. So maybe I can suggest some restaurants to go if your ask to me. Also I can cook most Japanese dish by myself.  So I can tell you how to cook it and we can cook together. I like Japanese food as well as Italian, Spanish, Korean, and Chinese. I like beer, sake（nihon-shu）, wine.  If you are intersted in sake, I have some sakes to drink with you.

I love cars. I love to go for driving with someone, seeing new cars, chatting about cars. 

I've met up with Couchsurfers many times. All of them are so kind and so nice. I'd like to see more and more people. 

Please feel free to contact to me. Thanks for reading my introduction.
